# A minimal small-cap cover can obstruct radial nonincrease strictification

Here is an actual three-fiber planar source and one inclusion-minimal
whole-space three-cap cover. Every cap has less than half the total mass.
Nevertheless, no nontrivial sufficiently small radial fiber change about
the common meeting section can simultaneously preserve convex compatibility,
avoid decreasing total mass, and avoid increasing any of those cap budgets.
The result includes higher-order radial paths, not only positive first-order
strictification. It makes no assertion about general shape or cap motions,
or about a cover below the OC threshold.

## 1. Exact actual source and cap fractions

Let K be the centered standard triangle with vertices

    (-1/3,-1/3), (2/3,-1/3), (-1/3,2/3),

and put J=[[-1,-2],[2,1]], A=(I+J/10)K, B=(I-J/10)K. Thus

    A=conv{(-7/30,-13/30),(2/3,-7/30),(-13/30,2/3)},
    B=conv{(-13/30,-7/30),(2/3,-13/30),(-7/30,2/3)}.

At bases -1,0,1 use A,D,B, respectively, where D=(A+B)/2.
Their lifted convex hull is full dimensional and has exactly these
integer fibers. The only excluded-target relation is the endpoint
midpoint relation, and it is equality. In counterclockwise order D has
the six vertices

    (-13/30,13/60), (-1/3,-1/3), (13/60,-13/30),
    (2/3,-1/3), (13/60,13/60), (-1/3,2/3).

The vertices of K occur in D, so K is contained in D. Direct determinants
or the shoelace formula give

    w=|A|=|B|=103/200,     W=|D|=13/20,
    M=2w+W=42/25.                                         (1)

Take the three cylindrical caps

    H_0={-x-y>=0}, H_1={x>=0}, H_2={y>=0}.                (2)

Their margins sum to zero, so they cover the entire ambient space,
including every integer fiber of every perturbed source. Each is
essential on the actual source: at base zero, the corresponding vertex
of K has strictly positive own margin and strictly negative other margins.

The determinant-one map R(x,y)=(-x-y,x) permutes the vertices of K,
commutes with J, and cyclically permutes the three cap margins. It
preserves each of A,B,D. All three cap fractions therefore agree within
each individual fiber. On A, the x-positive cap retains just one vertex;
its fraction is

    f=(2/3)^2 / [(9/10)(11/10)] = 400/891.                (3)

The same calculation on B interchanges the two denominators. The part
of D with x>=0 has the five counterclockwise vertices

    (0,-13/33), (13/60,-13/30), (2/3,-1/3),
    (13/60,13/60), (0,13/33).

Its area is 299/990, so the middle fraction is

    f_0=46/99,     f_0-f=14/891>0.                        (4)

Each entire mixed cap consequently has the same mass

    D_cap=2wf+Wf_0=6811/8910,
    D_cap/M=4865/10692 < 1/2.                             (5)

All cap boundaries have zero area in every fiber. These are genuine
closed ambient halfspaces, not a replacement by fiber-only tests.

## 2. Two actual support constraints

Scale the three fibers independently about zero by positive factors
r_-,r_0,r_+. Write

    a=(r_-+r_+)/2,     b=(r_--r_+)/2.

If the resulting array is an actual convex family, it must satisfy

    (r_- A+r_+ B)/2 subset r_0 D.                         (6)

For u=(1,-1), the supports of A,B are 9/10,11/10; for u=(2,1)
they are 11/10,9/10. In both directions h_D=1. Evaluating (6)
in these two directions gives

    r_0>=a-b/10,     r_0>=a+b/10,
    hence r_0>=a+|b|/10.                                (7)

The other support inequalities can impose additional restrictions.
Only the necessary inequalities (7) are used below.

## 3. No nearby finite radial improvement

Suppose |r_i-1|<1/10 for all three factors, the total mass M' does not
decrease, and no cap in (2) increases. Since radial dilation preserves
each through-origin cap fraction, exactly

    M'=2w(a^2+b^2)+Wr_0^2,
    D'_cap=f M'+W(f_0-f)r_0^2.                           (8)

Comparing (8) with (5), using M'>=M, D'_cap<=D_cap and f_0>f, gives
r_0^2<=1. Thus 9/10<r_0<=1. By (7), 0<a<=r_0-|b|/10, so

    M' <= M r_0^2 -(2w/5)r_0|b|+(101w/50)b^2.            (9)

Here |b|<1/10. If b is nonzero, the last two terms in (9) are at most

    w|b|[-9/25+101/500] = -(79/500)w|b| < 0.

Since r_0<=1, this contradicts M'>=M. If b=0, (7) gives a<=r_0<=1;
then the first equation in (8) and M'>=M force a=r_0=1. Hence all three
factors are exactly one.

This proves the claimed finite obstruction. It permits arbitrary
relative rates among the three scale changes, and so also excludes a
radial escape whose first derivative vanishes. It does not keep a merely
linearized compatibility condition in place of the actual inclusion.

## 4. Scope and relation to the cap-budget cone

At first order in the volume coordinates r_i=(1+t sigma_i)^(1/2),
the active canonical support direction has row proportional to
(-1/2,1,-1/2). Fixed total mass makes a positive active-gap derivative
force sigma_0>0. The derivative of any selected cap then has sign
W(f_0-f)sigma_0>0. This gives a concrete obstruction to the weak radial
cap-budget cone even though the selected caps form a whole-space cover
and every budget is below half the mass. The finite argument above is
strictly stronger than that first-order observation.

There is also an explicit Farkas certificate in the notation of
`candidate f0b371d38574bbcc`. Use the
active support row a=(-1/3,2/3,-1/3), the mass row w_vec=(w,W,w),
and any one of the identical cap rows c=(wf,Wf_0,wf). Direct rational
substitution gives

    a=(142560/1339)c-(194600/4017)w_vec.

The cap coefficient is strictly positive. Multiplying by a proposed
fixed-mass direction with c.sigma<=0 contradicts a.sigma>0. This is
an exact dual certificate using one actual cap and one actual active
compatibility row, not an abstract incidence-only counterexample.

General affine vertex motions, changes in cap directions, and motion
of the meeting section are outside this radial obstruction. The common
centroid path is actually zero: the threefold rotation has only the zero
fixed vector, so every fiber centroid is zero. In particular the source
is safely above its OC requirement by an elementary argument. At (0,0),
every closed through-halfspace contains the centroid of the middle fiber
and at least one endpoint fiber. Ordinary Grunbaum on those fibers gives
normalized depth at least

    Gamma_2 (W+w)/M = 233/756 > Gamma_2/2 = 2/9.

Vertical caps obey the same bound directly. No maximum-depth value or
failure of OC is asserted. The obstruction only shows that whole-space
coverage and a below-half budget do not by themselves make radial
nonincrease strictification possible.
